summary.headline: Novus Loyalty H1 FY27 revenue rose to about ₹98 crore (vs ₹71 crore in H1 FY26), with ~35-40% growth; AutoPay 80.87% acquisition pending funding in June 2027.
summary.overview: Management reported H1 FY27 revenue of about ₹98 crore against ₹71 crore in H1 FY26, with growth across all four revenue lines. The company is debt-free and says EBITDA and PAT margins are improving. It has signed an SPA to acquire 80.87% of AutoPay, a payments company, to gain payment and PPI licence access. Management pointed to a Dubai subsidiary, African bank wins, and an AI platform (Noxcy AI) as growth drivers. Call answers flagged H1 inventory and unbilled work build-up and gave H2 guidance in line with H1.

financial_highlights.value: ~₹7.5 crore (also cited as ~₹9.5 crore in later answers)

financial_highlights.metric: Digital vouchers / gift vouchers H1 FY27

financial_highlights.value: more than ₹14 crore (PAT margin ~13.8%, vs ~21.9% earlier)

segments.name: Technology (platform/SaaS)
segments.commentary: About 7% of gross revenue and ~₹7.5-9.5 crore in H1 FY27; ~90% of clients on SaaS, ~10% on-premise. Treated as 100% net revenue.

segments.name: Redemption engine
segments.commentary: About 39% of gross revenue, ~₹36 crore in H1 FY27; gross margin about 16-18% due to direct costs.

segments.name: Merchant promotion
segments.commentary: About 6% of gross revenue, a little over ₹5 crore in H1 FY27; management expects it to drive higher profits, with 100% flowing to gross margin.

segments.name: Digital/gift vouchers
segments.commentary: About 48% of gross revenue, ~₹49 crore in H1 FY27; gross margin only 5-7% without a PPI licence.

segments.name: AutoPay (proposed subsidiary)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue ₹102 crore and PAT above ₹14 crore; IRCTC is the core customer, with DMRC/Saathi app onboarding depressing margins. Management guides 17-20% PAT margin long term and 15-20% growth.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27 expected to be in line with H1, or better; management said it will not be lower.
Dubai/Middle East: ~$1 million revenue in FY27 and ~$2 million (₹12-15 crore) next year; GCC revenue expected to begin within six months.
Africa: ~$200,000 billed so far (Bank of Abyssinia and another bank); target ~$400,000 in FY27.
Targets: consolidated ~₹500 crore by FY29 and ₹600-650 crore by FY30.
Base business organic CAGR ~15% (ex-AutoPay); AutoPay expected to grow at least 15-20% a year.
Noxcy AI: break-even on its cost in 1.5-2 years; clients expected to pay separately in future.
capex_capacity: AutoPay funding: ~20% via share swap, ~₹40 crore from internal accruals and IPO proceeds, and ~₹40-45 crore due in June 2027, possibly funded through a preferential issue.
Central Bank of India contract (~₹88 crore over 5 years): ~10% technology and ~90% redemption; net revenue ~₹3-4 crore in year one, roughly doubling yearly.
Planned small US subsidiary or acquisition of a small digital agency to serve US and Australia clients; ~$1 million revenue targeted there next year.
Dubai subsidiary set up with about 3 hires; GCC access established.
demand_pricing: Seasonality is minimal: summer +5-10%, Diwali +2-5%, New Year higher; H2 FY26 was about ₹56 crore vs ₹71 crore in H1 FY27, attributed to client-driven campaign timing.
Main domestic competitor: Loyalty Rewards (BillDesk-owned). International competitors: GIIFT, Concilion, Vernost.
Client base: ~100 enterprise clients, 5+ crore customers, 150+ crore transactions a month; NPCI RuPay credit card programme for 5-6 years.
Unbilled work and inventory built up in H1: about ₹2 crore WIP (NPCI, Bank of Abyssinia) plus unbilled redemption and merchant promotion income, and unsold gift voucher inventory.

qa_highlights.question: Why did AutoPay PAT margin fall from ~21.9% to 13.8%, and what is sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the fall to DMRC/Saathi app R&D, a ₹1.5 crore MMG payment to metros and slow revenue ramp. It expects 17-20% margins over the long run.

qa_highlights.question: What is the rationale for the ~₹130 crore AutoPay valuation and expected growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Valuation was set after a fair-value exercise and talks with sellers, with PAT history as a consideration. AutoPay expected to grow at least 15-20% a year; an EOI was submitted for an Indian Railways transit loyalty system.

qa_highlights.question: Which verticals will drive revenue and profit going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Redemption and gift vouchers will grow in revenue, but merchant promotion is expected to drive higher profit. Gross margins: technology 100%, redemption 16-18%, merchant promotion 100%, gift vouchers 5-7%.

qa_highlights.question: Is there seasonality, and why was H2 FY26 lower than H1?
qa_highlights.answer: No material seasonality; H2 FY26 weakness was attributed to client campaign timing rather than a seasonal pattern.

qa_highlights.question: What is the organic base-business CAGR excluding AutoPay?
qa_highlights.answer: About 15% for the base business. Management expects 15-20% organic growth on AutoPay if it adds clients on the same technology.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory build up in H1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Mix of about ₹2 crore unbilled WIP awaiting POs, unbilled redemption and merchant promotion income (30-45 day settlement, refund risk), and unsold gift voucher inventory.

risks_watch: AutoPay margin compression: PAT margin fell to ~13.8% from ~21.9%; the 17-20% target depends on DMRC/Saathi revenue ramping up.
Funding: ~₹40-45 crore payment due June 2027; preferential issue and IPO proceeds planned.
Working capital: unbilled WIP, unbilled redemption and merchant income, and voucher inventory built up in H1 FY27.
International execution: US/Australia entry depends on a subsidiary or partner; Dubai and Africa revenue ramp is still early.
Revenue concentration: large bank/NPCI contracts and client-driven campaign timing drive lumpy half-yearly revenue.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth, AI and international plans, but answers on AutoPay margins and unbilled inventory were detailed and somewhat hedged. Several answers were loosely structured and figures were restated inconsistently (for example, technology revenue of ₹7.5 crore vs ₹9.5 crore).
key_quotes: So, we, have a stable business of the IRCTC, but the next the DMRC one, that still need to kick in, and then you'll see margin improvements going forward in that business as well, right?

Planned small US subsidiary or acquisition of small digital agency to serve US and Australia clients

growth.why: Management guides H2 FY27 in line with H1 (~₹98 Cr), a held not raised outlook, and a ~15% organic base-business CAGR, with the Dubai (~$1M FY27) and Africa (~$400K FY27 target) wins plus the Central Bank of India contract (~₹88 Cr over 5 years) as partial backing; no physical capacity additions are disclosed.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management says EBITDA and PAT margins are improving, but AutoPay PAT margin fell to ~13.8% from ~21.9% and redemption/voucher gross margins are only 16-18% and 5-7%, so the gain depends on mix shift toward merchant promotion (100% gross margin) and AutoPay DMRC/Saathi ramp.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No physical plant or line capacity is disclosed; the additions are a Dubai subsidiary already set up with ~3 hires and a planned small US subsidiary or digital agency acquisition, with the Central Bank of India contract (~Rs 88 Cr over 5 years) adding delivery load.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides a ~15% organic base-business CAGR and H2 FY27 in line with H1 (~Rs 98 Cr), with Dubai ~$1M revenue in FY27 and Africa targeted at ~$400K in FY27 (~$200K billed so far).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: The ~Rs 40-45 Cr AutoPay payment due June 2027 may be funded via a preferential issue, and a small US subsidiary or agency acquisition is planned, but no capex amount or plant is named and the company is debt-free.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: H2 FY27 is guided only in line with H1 (~Rs 98 Cr) and held rather than raised, while H2 FY26 was ~Rs 56 Cr vs H1 FY27 ~Rs 71 Cr on campaign timing.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H2 FY26 was ~Rs 56 Cr vs H1 FY27 ~Rs 71 Cr from lumpy campaign timing, and unbilled WIP (~Rs 2 Cr) and inventory build-up raise collection risk, though management said H2 will not be lower.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Noxcy AI platform is in place with break-even on its cost in 1.5-2 years, and clients are expected to pay separately in future, though no launch date or revenue figure was given.

rows.label: Dubai/GCC and Africa revenue ramp
rows.why: Dubai ~$1M revenue in FY27 and ~$2M (Rs 12-15 Cr) next year; Africa ~$200K billed so far against a ~$400K FY27 target, with GCC revenue expected within six months.

rows.label: AutoPay 80.87% acquisition and funding
rows.why: SPA signed for 80.87% of AutoPay (FY26 revenue Rs 102 Cr, PAT above Rs 14 Cr), with ~20% via share swap and ~Rs 40-45 Cr due in June 2027, possibly through a preferential issue.

rows.label: AutoPay margin recovery to 17-20%
rows.why: PAT margin fell to ~13.8% from ~21.9% on DMRC/Saathi R&D and a Rs 1.5 Cr MMG payment, and recovery depends on a slow revenue ramp that is not yet visible.

tone.note: Management was confident on the growth, AI and international story, but hedged on AutoPay margin compression and H1 unbilled inventory, and restated technology revenue inconsistently (Rs 7.5 Cr vs Rs 9.5 Cr); analysts pressed on margins and working capital.
